title: Start from the generic "New" button and choose what to create
prompt:
# Story 1: Start from the generic "New" button and choose what to create

- **Story**: XXX-new-document-prompt
- **Created**: 2026-11-09
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open the workspace, press "New", see the prompt for a story, tick "Mark as architectural enabler" and see the box turn green and
  the ADR panel appear, untick it and see the story prompt again, then press "New" with a draft on screen and see the confirmation.

## Story

As a team member, I want one "New" button and one prompt where I choose whether I am writing a story or an architectural enabler, so that I
start either from the same place and never look for a different button for each.

## Acceptance tests

The "New" button

- [ ] **Given** the workspace, **Then** the header of the tree ("Files" and the project name) has, on its right, a round-cornered button with
  a plus icon whose accessible name and tooltip are **"New"**. It is the same whether a story or an enabler will be written, and it is not
  named after either.
- [ ] **Given** the button, **When** the user presses it, **Then** any open file is closed, the prompt shows in the middle with the
  earlier messages hidden (not deleted), the focus goes to the box, and the main menu is a rail of icons.
- [ ] **Given** a draft is waiting for approval, **When** the user presses "New", **Then** a confirmation asks "Discard the draft that is waiting
  for approval?". **When** the user confirms, **Then** the draft is dropped and the above happens. **When** the user does not, **Then** nothing
  changes.
- [ ] **Given** the user typed text, ticked the box or chose links, **When** the user presses "New", **Then** they are kept (the button resets the
  screen and the conversation, not the box).
- [ ] **Given** the folders of the tree, **Then** "New" does not open or close any.

The prompt

- [ ] **Given** the prompt with no conversation, **Then** it shows a sparkles icon, the title "Which story shall we tell today?", the line
  "Describe what a user needs. Claude drafts the story, and once you approve it BWYN creates its folder.", the box, and three examples (below).
- [ ] **Given** the box, **Then** its placeholder is "Describe a user story...", it grows with its text up to 200 px and then scrolls, and it
  has the focus when the workspace opens, when "New" is pressed, and when an example is pressed.
- [ ] **Given** the examples, **Then** they are, in this order, "As a returning customer, I want to sign in with my email and password, so
  that I can see my orders.", "As a project lead, I want to export the project report as a PDF file." and "Set up continuous integration for the
  frontend build.". **When** the user presses one, **Then** it fills the box (replacing what was there), the focus stays in the box, and the
  checkbox is **not** changed. The examples are shown only while the conversation is empty.
- [ ] **Given** a file is open, **Then** the prompt is a narrow column (26 rem) on the right of the file, with the same box, the Link button
  and the checkbox; with no file open it takes the middle. The title and the line are shown only in the middle.
- [ ] **Given** no model is connected, **Then** the banner and the caption of `story-architectural-enablers.md` (story 1) show here too.

The checkbox

- [ ] **Given** the prompt that creates something new, **Then** below the box, next to the Link button, a checkbox named **"Mark as
  architectural enabler"**, with a zap icon, shows **not ticked**.
- [ ] **Given** the checkbox is not ticked, **Then** the prompt is a story prompt: the placeholder is "Describe a user story...", the box has a
  faint border (indigo while it has the focus), no ADR panel shows, the Link button offers ADRs, and the send button is named "Draft story".
- [ ] **Given** the user ticks the checkbox, **Then** the label turns green, the placeholder becomes "Describe the architectural enabler...", the
  box gets a green border, a green panel "Derives from an Accepted ADR (required)" appears inside the box, the Link button no longer offers
  ADRs, and the send button is named "Draft architectural enabler" (the enabler stories describe the panel and what it needs to send).
- [ ] **Given** the title and the line above the box, **Then** they do not change when the box is ticked.
- [ ] **Given** the checkbox is ticked and the user unticks it, **Then** the story prompt is back. The text in the box is kept in both
  directions. The ADRs that were chosen stay chosen, and are used again if the user ticks it again, but they are never sent with a story.
- [ ] **Given** the checkbox is ticked, **Then** the enablers that every story gets by default (below, story 6) are taken out of the links, and
  **When** it is unticked, **Then** they are in them again.
- [ ] **Given** the user sends, **Then** the composer is reset: the box is empty, the checkbox is not ticked, the ADRs and the links are
  cleared (the links go back to the default enablers).
- [ ] **Given** a draft is on screen, or an open **enabler** is the target of the prompt (`story-architectural-enablers.md`, story 7), **Then**
  the checkbox and the Link button are not shown: what is being written cannot change kind.
- [ ] **Given** the keyboard, **Then** the checkbox is reached with Tab and ticked with Space, and a visible ring shows the focus.
- [ ] **Given** the checkbox, **Then** it is a native checkbox inside its label, so that pressing the label ticks it.

What sending does

- [ ] **Given** the box is not ticked and has text (not only spaces), **Then** the send button is enabled, named "Draft story", whatever the ADRs
  and links. **Given** it is ticked, **Then** it also needs a chosen ADR (`story-architectural-enablers.md`, story 1).
- [ ] **Given** the box is not ticked, **When** the user presses Enter (not Shift+Enter, not while an input method composes), **Then** a story is
  drafted (story 2). **Given** it is ticked, **Then** an enabler is drafted.

## Business rules and constraints

- The prompt is **one** component with **one** "New" button. What is created depends only on the checkbox when the prompt is sent.
- The default is a **story**. The enabler is the exception, and it is chosen by ticking.
- A draft cannot change kind. To change it, the user discards the draft and starts again.
- The spike keeps the heading and the line of the prompt as they are for a story, whatever the checkbox says (see "Something to decide").
- Everything on the screen is reachable by keyboard.

## Out of scope

- Drafting a story (story 2), and approving (story 4). Drafting an enabler (`story-architectural-enablers.md`).
- The panel of ADRs and the rules about them, which belong to the enabler stories.
- The Link button and its list (`story-link-picker.md`), and the default enablers (story 6).
- Two buttons ("New story", "New enabler"), a menu on "New", and keyboard shortcuts for it.
- Keeping the text, the tick or the links of the box after the page is reloaded.

## Tasks

- [ ] Rename the tree header's button to the generic "New" (accessible name and tooltip), and keep what it does: confirm, discard, close the
  file, hide the earlier messages, focus, collapse the menu. It does not touch the box or the folders.
- [ ] Give the prompt its story default: title, line, placeholder "Describe a user story...", the send label "Draft story", the three
  examples, and the 200 px growing box.
- [ ] Add the checkbox "Mark as architectural enabler" to the composer, with its pill, its zap icon and its ticked and unticked looks.
- [ ] Make the ticked state show the enabler prompt: the placeholder, the green border, the ADR panel, the Link button without ADRs, and the
  send label and rule. Keep the state of the box, the ADRs and the links across ticking and unticking.
- [ ] Hide the checkbox and the Link button while a draft is on screen or an enabler is the target.
- [ ] Reset the box, the tick, the ADRs and the links when something is sent.
- [ ] Test: the button's name, "New" with and without a draft and with typed text, the examples, the tick and untick (placeholder, border,
  panel, send rule, kept text and ADRs), the reset after sending, and the hidden checkbox while a draft is on screen.

tasks.text: Rename the tree header button to "New" (accessible name and tooltip) and verify it confirms before discarding a waiting draft, closes any open file, hides earlier messages, and moves focus to the box without touching the box content or the folders.

Implement the story-default prompt: sparkles icon, title, line, placeholder "Describe a user story...", send button labelled "Draft story", three examples shown only while the conversation is empty, and a growing box capped at 200 px.
Implement the narrow-column layout (26 rem) when a file is open, hiding the title and the line.
Add the "Mark as architectural enabler" checkbox with its zap icon and its unticked default appearance.

Implement the ticked state: green label, placeholder "Describe the architectural enabler...", green border, ADR panel placeholder, Link button without ADRs, send button labelled "Draft architectural enabler"; preserve box text, ADR choices, and links across ticking and unticking.
Hide the checkbox and the Link button when a draft is on screen or an enabler is the target of the prompt.
Reset the box, the checkbox, the ADRs, and the links when the prompt is sent.

Write Jest tests covering: button accessible name; "New" with and without a waiting draft; "New" with typed text (text is kept); examples fill the box and disappear after a conversation starts; checkbox ticked and unticked (placeholder, border, panel, send label, text and ADR preservation); reset after sending; checkbox hidden while a draft is on screen.
